_note: The guided intro, in order. title and text are what the card says. highlight names the real control to outline: {button: text of a top bar button}, {group: a node group} (a window, the map mode bar, the event feed), or none. done is what completes the step: {command: class name} (a command the player gave), {signal: camera | province_selected | mode_changed | game_saved}, {mode: [map modes]}, {window: group of a window that must be open} or {ack: true} (the Got it button). requires: fleet skips the step for a nation with no fleet. Every step can be skipped.

steps.title: Move around the map
steps.text: Hold W, A, S and D to pan, or drag with the middle mouse button. Turn the wheel to zoom in and out.

steps.title: Select a province
steps.text: Click any province. The panel at the top left tells you who owns it, how many people live there and what it produces.

steps.title: Read a map mode
steps.text: The buttons at the bottom left recolour the map: who owns what, the economy, population, armies, terrain. Click one (keys 1 to 6 do the same).

steps.title: Build something
steps.text: Open the Construction panel (B), pick a building, and click a green province on the map to build it there. It costs industrial capacity (IC), not money, and takes at least a few weeks; your civilian factories set how much IC you have each day. It shows in the queue at the bottom right.

steps.title: Raise an army
steps.text: Open the Military window (M), pick one of your provinces and train a unit. Units cost money and recruits, and form an army where they were raised.

steps.title: Equip your army
steps.text: Units need arms and guns, and the guns need shells; without them they fight worse. Open the Economy window (E), its Production tab, and move a factory between the Arms, Artillery and Shells lines with the plus and minus buttons. Items cost industrial capacity, iron, coal and nitrates, not money. Your economy law, on the Overview tab, trades civilian output for military output once you are at war.

steps.title: Move an army
steps.text: Click an army to select it, then right-click a province to send it there. Drag a box to select several at once. Time is paused: press Space to start the clock, and armies will march.

steps.title: Set a front
steps.text: With armies selected, use the bar at the bottom of the screen to draw a front: a line of provinces your army holds against an enemy. Armies assigned to a front defend it.

steps.title: Improve relations
steps.text: Open the Diplomacy window (F), choose a nation and improve relations with it. Diplomatic effort costs diplomacy points, shown in the top bar.

steps.title: Read the event feed
steps.text: News appears at the top of the map: battles, wars, treaties, ships sunk and blockades. Keep an eye on it while the clock runs.

steps.title: Send a fleet
steps.text: Open the Navy panel (N), select a fleet, then right-click a patch of sea to send it there. Fleets stationed in the right waters can cut an enemy's trade.

steps.title: See the blockade
steps.text: Press 7 or use the Sea map mode at the bottom left to see who controls each sea zone, and which ports are blockaded.

steps.title: Save your game
steps.text: Press F5 to quick save, or F6 to open the save window. The game also saves itself on the first of every month. That is everything: good luck!
